text:
mina: heads-up — CI started failing on the new JS SDK ESM publish. Vitest in the edge runtime job throws a bunch of ERR_REQUIRE_ESM and also some weird mock shape errors for auth.retry. stack points to node_modules/node-fetch/dist/index.cjs (?!).

lucas: weird. node-fetch published ESM-only recently and some packages still import the CJS path. Are you bundling or using deps.inline?

mina: vitest.config.ts snippet: 
```
export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    environment: 'edge-runtime',
    deps: { inline: ['@redwood/sdk'] },
    globals: true,
  }
})
```
We alias `@redwood/sdk` -> src for local DX. CI doesn't alias and sees dist with conditional exports.

anya: two quick hits: 1) edge runtime sets a different resolver (vite) and sometimes pulls an unexpected subpath from package.exports; 2) our auth retry helper does a dynamic require fallback: `const fetchLib = tryRequire('node-fetch') || globalThis.fetch` — that tryRequire path can cause CJS/ESM mismatch on consumers.

mina: aha — our retry helper uses `require('node-fetch')` guarded by try/catch. In ESM consumers that path isn't used, but Vitest's edge runner still tries to resolve require at runtime during mocking and runs into ESM-only package.

lucas: replace tryRequire with an ESM-friendly loader like: `const fetchLib = (typeof globalThis.fetch === 'function') ? globalThis.fetch : await import('node-fetch').then(m=>m.default || m)` — and make the helper async where needed. That avoids require() paths.

mina: good call. But we also have test mocks that do `vi.mock('@redwood/sdk/auth', ()=>({ getToken: ()=> 'x' }))` which fails because the real module is ESM default-exported. Mocks expect named exports.

anya: prefer `vi.mock('@redwood/sdk/auth', async () => { const mod = await vi.importActual('@redwood/sdk/auth'); return { ...mod, getToken: vi.fn(()=> 'x') } })` — that preserves shapes and works with ESM.

mina: tried that locally, passes. CI still fails in matrix job node:20 with `SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'export'` pointing to `dist/esm/utils.mjs` being loaded by a CJS consumer.

lucas: search for stray `require('@redwood/sdk')` in test helpers or setup files. If a setup file uses CommonJS the resolver will pick require path.

mina: found `const sdk = require('@redwood/sdk')` in test/setup-legacy.js. Oof.

anya: there you go. Two options: 1) convert setup-legacy.js to ESM (rename to .mjs or use type:module and use import). 2) publish a tiny cjs bridge in the package root for tests: e.g., `auth.cjs` that does `module.exports = require('./dist/cjs/auth.js')` — but that's extra publishing work.

mina: converting helpers seems cleaner for us. Also we should stop aliasing to src locally because it hides the conditional exports behavior — that was the onboarding friction: new hires run locally, everything works, then CI breaks.

lucas: agree. For vitest specifically, add `resolve: { conditions: ['import','node'] }` so vite will prefer the correct export condition. Also ensure `deps.inline` includes the SDK so Vite bundles it instead of letting node resolve at runtime.

paul: one addition on retry/auth shape: if your retry wrapper re-exports functions, ensure you support both `default` and named shapes for compatibility: e.g., `export * from './auth.js'; export {default} from './auth.js'` or add `auth.node.cjs` that re-exports to help require() callers. That buys downstream time while we migrate tests.

mina: plan: 1) convert legacy test helpers to ESM; 2) change auth retry loader to import() pattern; 3) update mocks to use vi.importActual; 4) add vitest.resolve.conditions and inline deps in CI config; 5) add a small debug job that prints resolver choices using `node -e "console.log(require.resolve('@redwood/sdk/auth'))"` and `node -e "import('@redwood/sdk/auth').then(()=>console.log('import ok'))"`.

lucas: also add CI matrix for node 18/20 to catch resolver differences early.

anya: if you want I can open a tiny PR for the auth loader change and an example vi.mock for the auth module. saves time for the onboarding docs too.

mina: please do — that'll help the new hires who hit this when running the sample app tests. thanks! :sparkles:

dev-bot: CI re-run for job "edge-tests" requested by mina.

paul: tl;dr: root cause was mixed module loaders + require() in retry helper + alias hiding exports -> fixed by ESM-first helpers, dynamic import for optional dependencies, and ESM-aware mocks.
